note: Every pre-registered study run on TradePro. Gates were COMMITTED TO GIT BEFORE each run — the commit sha is on each entry so the claim is checkable, not trusted. A study with a FAIL verdict is kept, not deleted: the negative results are the point.

studies.title: Wheel CSP — 200-SMA primary-trend floor
studies.question: Does refusing to sell puts on names below their 200-SMA fix the wheel's single-name drawdown?
studies.prediction: G4 passes (the floor blocks the META-class entry); G3 is the risk.
studies.headline: G3 CAGR 7.61% (v2 8.25%), G4 full-period META −71.4%
studies.why: The trend floor did not save it. Worse, the harness had never graded G4 on the FULL window — v2's celebrated '8/9 PASS' was flattered by a gate that was never scored. Entry filters cannot reach the failure mechanism, which is being assigned into a decliner and holding it.

studies.title: Support/resistance levels — do they predict anything?
studies.question: When price touches one of the levels drawn on our charts, does it reject more often than an identically-placed line that is NOT a level?
studies.prediction: G1/G2 fail with an edge of 0-3 points.
studies.verdict: FAIL — the chart lines carry no edge
studies.headline: 76,260 touch events. Resistance edge −0.34 pts, support −1.26 pts vs placebo.
studies.why: Both edges are NEGATIVE: a randomly-placed line predicted the next 5 bars marginally better than a real pivot level. The unconditional 5-bar down-rate is 45.50% against a 45.19% resistance rejection rate — touching resistance tells you nothing drift does not. Well-powered, not a small sample.

gates.test: Edge same sign in both halves

studies.title: Ichimoku — support-distance entry filter
studies.question: ICH's live record is −$376 at a 20% win rate with losses 4.7x wins. Does refusing entries within 2 ATR of a support level fix it?
studies.prediction: G1/G2/G5 pass, G3 fails — better trades, less money.
studies.headline: Win rate +1.9 pts (needed +4). Avg/trade +9% relative (needed +50%). Loss/win ratio got WORSE.
studies.why: A forward-return study on 25,120 entries had shown a clean 2.25x separation at 2 ATR. It did not survive real entries, real exits and costs. Prediction was wrong in the opposite direction — the per-trade improvement barely exists.

studies.title: Ichimoku — exit rule variants
studies.question: Three entry ideas failed. The exit is 'close<cloud_bottom OR tenkan<kijun' — tenkan is a 5-period line against kijun's 32, so it fires on any pullback. Is the fast leg what cuts winners?
studies.prediction: B (cloud-only) passes G1/G2/G3; G4 is the risk.
studies.headline: Removing the tenkan<kijun leg: total +41%, mean/trade 2.46x, median hold 19→34 bars, tail concentration FELL 55%→51%.
studies.why: Confirmed by the control: variant D (kijun trail) exits fastest at a 6-bar median and is the WORST on every measure with a 72% tail share — which is the live sleeves' behaviour reproduced deliberately. Caveat: win rate falls 39.1%→34.7%, and this DEPARTS from the trader's documented spec so it needs a parity test before adoption.

studies.title: Ichimoku — profit targets, win rate as a HARD gate
studies.question: Owner: 'a winrate of 34-35% is a no-go for an algo platform.' Can profit targets lift the win rate without gutting the tail?
studies.prediction: H (scale-out) passes all four; E (+10% target) passes G1 and fails G2.
studies.headline: Best win rate 44.2% (E), which loses money vs baseline. Best overall G (min-hold+20% target): 43.2% win, beats baseline total, and cuts tail dependence 54%→23%.
studies.why: No variant reached 45%. The prediction was WRONG — H (scale-out) was the worst variant, below baseline. The conclusion registered in advance applies: this signal family cannot deliver ≥45%, so the choice is accept ~43% or change family. Notably G more than halves tail dependence, which addresses the fragility behind the win-rate objection.

studies.title: Mean-reversion swing candidates
studies.question: Owner wants candidates to get into and out of quickly with a high hit rate. Ichimoku cannot do that — its edge IS the long hold and the tail. Can mean reversion?
studies.prediction: M1 (RSI2) + X1 strongest; G5 (worst trade) is where I expect trouble.
studies.verdict: PARTIAL — confirmed on clean data, one gate unmet
studies.headline: M2+X2 (2.5σ dip in an uptrend, target the 20-day mean, −8% stop): 62.4% win, 4-bar median hold, worst −12.5%. RE-RUN on the cleaned store after 6 wrong-venue symbols were dropped: 2,400 trades, 62.4% win, +0.77%/trade — IDENTICAL. Fails G4 only (tail 26% vs 25%).
studies.why: Completely different profile from Ichimoku: 65% win vs 39%, 4-bar holds vs 41+ bars needed, and profit spread across many trades rather than 54% from the top 1%. A stop fixes the worst trade (−34%→−16%) but breaks G4 by concentrating the tail (25%→37%) — a real trade-off, not a fix. IMPORTANT: the first pass was contaminated by corrupt bars; mean reversion is uniquely exposed because its premise is BUY THE CRASH, and a fake −60% print is exactly what it buys. Numbers here are post-guard. RE-RUN 22 Aug against the store after another dev's wrong-venue remediation, dropping the 6 symbols still carrying a different instrument's series (MTUM 18.9x, QUAL 16.7x, VIXY 16.6x, USMV 14.5x, VLUE 9.5x, BILL 6.2x their recent medians). Only 13 of 2,413 trades came from them and every headline number was unchanged — the edge was never riding on corrupt data. Those symbols are now DROPPED and NAMED by the live screen rather than silently included.

studies.title: Momentum — pullback in an uptrend, trailing + hard stop
studies.question: The mean-reversion screen refuses to buy strength — MU on Friday (966.78, 69% above its 200-SMA) triggered nothing, its entry sat 24% lower. Is there a tradeable edge in continuation, with calculated risk?
studies.prediction: C (hard −8%) passes all six; D (−6%) passes G5 but fails G1; the risk is G4.
studies.headline: Pullback to the 10-SMA in an uptrend, 8% trailing stop plus a hard −8% initial stop: 5,815 trades · 47.0% win · +1.53%/trade · 34-bar median hold · worst −14.7%. The −10% variant also passes.
studies.why: v1 proved the family's edge REQUIRES the hold — a trailing stop earns +1.9%/trade over 32-35 bars, while forcing 10 bars costs two thirds of it. G3 was therefore changed from ≤20 to ≤40 bars as a DECLARED scope change, written down before the v2 run: momentum is accepted as a longer-hold sleeve running alongside the 4-day Swing screen, not as a substitute. The hard stop cut the worst case from −33.3% to −14.7% for 1.3 points of win rate and 0.07%/trade — cheap insurance. Prediction was correct: C passed, D (−6%) failed G1 at 42.9% by stopping out of trades that later worked. NOTE the first run was contaminated (−98% worst cases): capping total return is the WRONG guard for a 30-bar hold, since a real winner can exceed it; the guard belongs on the HOLD (reject any session moving >35% mid-trade).

studies.title: Momentum v3 — does entry-bar volume add anything?
studies.prediction: G7 (must survive a TIME split and a SYMBOL split) is where this most likely dies — under 50% that anything passes G1-G6 and then survives it. D (>=1.2x) fails G1 on trade count. C (>=1.0x) marginal on G4, median between -0.1% and +0.4%.
studies.headline: Entry-bar volume looked monotonic on the full sample (<0.7x: 45.4% win; >1.2x: 52.2%). It is a REGIME, not an edge: in the first half of the record, filtering on volume makes the strategy WORSE, and worst for the strictest filter. D goes +2.24%→+1.62% pre-2020 and +2.17%→+3.50% after. All three variants fail G7.

gates.result: fails the time split — inverts pre-2020

studies.verdictLabel: REJECTED — all three variants fail G7
studies.predictionGraded: 3 of 5 correct. The one that mattered — that G7 would kill it — was called before the run.
studies.why: D passed the symbol split cleanly — either split ALONE would have shipped it. Requiring two independent cuts is what caught it. No untouched hold-out existed (the effect was found on the full sample), which is stated in the gates file rather than glossed. Consequence: no volume filter ships; v2 stands. Volume is shown in the drill-down as context labelled a failed filter. Also corrected the screen's published evidence — 5,815/47.0%/+1.53%/-14.7% predated the _tradeable fix and included futures and indices; the true figures are 5,396 trades, 48.8% win, +2.20%/trade, median -0.33%, worst -29.7%.

studies.title: Mean reversion v2 — first reproducible Swing measurement
studies.prediction: Not a fresh pre-registration — graded against v1's gates, unchanged, on a defined universe and cleaned data.
studies.headline: 1,270 trades · 66.2% win · +0.88%/trade · median +1.91% · worst -17.7% · hold 7. G4 (top-1% tail) 19.9% of net vs the 25% ceiling — v1 FAILED this at 26% and shipped anyway. Passes a two-split test that rejected momentum v3 and the intraday dip study the same day.
studies.verdictLabel: ALL SIX gates pass, incl. G4 which v1 failed
studies.why: The v1 harness did not exist — written in a scratch dir, never committed, and its surviving log does not record hold length, so '4 bars' traced to no artifact. This is therefore the FIRST reproducible measurement, not a reconciliation. Trade count halved because v1's universe included futures and indices. The worst trade got WORSE (-12.5% -> -17.7%) as a CORRECTION: stops now fill at min(stop, open), because a gap through a stop does not fill at the stop — modelling the fill at the trigger gave exactly -8.0% in every variant, a stop that never slips. No exit convention reproduces v1's 4-bar hold; all four give 7-10 and all four pass every gate.

studies.title: Post-earnings cash-secured put — no market filter
studies.question: Is selling a put AFTER a report that dropped >=8% better than selling puts at random?
studies.prediction: G3 (beats the null) is where I expect trouble — the earnings set is concentrated in volatile names and volatile weeks.
studies.headline: n=284, win 87.0%, mean +1.19%/trade, p5 -5.48%; NULL was -0.15%
studies.why: The prediction was WRONG in the strategy's favour: G3 passed decisively (+1.25pt over a same-filtered null of -0.15%), so the earnings trigger does real work. It failed on sample size and on consistency: half 1 (2020-22) returned +0.75% with p5 -13.69% against half 2's +1.37%/-5.21%. Half 1 holds the 2022 bear market; a short put is long delta and behaved like it.

studies.title: Post-earnings put + SPY 200-SMA market-regime filter
studies.question: Does entering only while SPY is above its 200-day average fix V1's failure?
studies.prediction: W6 passes; W7 (retention) is the risk — earnings drops cluster in bad markets, so the filter may 'work' by refusing to trade.
studies.headline: n=229, win 89.5%, mean +1.29%, worst -23.4% (was -54.1%); retained 81% of events
studies.verdict: PASS (8/8) — PAPER FORWARD TEST, NOT FUNDED
studies.why: Prediction wrong again in the strategy's favour: retention was 81% against a 60% floor. Half 1 improved from +0.75%/p5 -13.69% to +1.43%/p5 +0.00%. THE WEAK PASS, recorded not fixed: W6 ('2022 must not lose') passed on NINE events — the filter removed 41 of 2022's 50 drops, so 'fixed' is thinly evidenced. Earnings history starts Oct 2020, so both halves sit in ONE regime.

studies.title: Intraday short strangle, low-VIX filter — BANKNIFTY, 18 years
studies.question: Owner's live Indian strategy: does a fixed-width intraday short strangle, entered only on low-VIX days and closed EOD, make money?
studies.prediction: G5 is the risk — the early half contains 2008 and the taper tantrum.
studies.headline: 18y: LOSES. mean -2,469/trade on low-VIX days; -20.5M total across all days
studies.why: An earlier 2-year run (2024-26) showed +1,464/trade and did NOT generalise: 2008-2016 mean -3,298, 2017-2026 mean -1,670 — losing even at a 72.4% win rate, which is the clearest demonstration that win rate is not evidence for premium selling. Two things changed: the VIX quartile moved from a whole-sample boundary (lookahead) to a TRAILING one, and the sample gained 2008-2016. CAVEAT NOT YET TESTED: strikes were held at a fixed +/-0.87%, which at 2008-era volatility is near-the-money — a far riskier trade than the owner would place. Volatility-scaled strikes are the next test and may change the verdict.
